title: Veterans Pension Net Worth — Insurance Premiums by Age of the Premium Reports
content:
## Insurance premiums counted in Veterans Pension net worth

Insurance premiums for net worth count by how recently they were reported: medical expense reports received three to eleven whole months before the redetermination count as premiums at their total; when none was received in that span and some were received twelve to twenty-three whole months before, the standard Medicare Part B premium for twelve months for each member of the household the rate category covers is counted instead; otherwise premiums add nothing. Reports are aged by the whole months from the day VA received them to the redetermination.

**Q. Which medical expense reports count as premiums at their total?**
A. Those received 3 to 11 whole months before the redetermination — received within the last 12 whole months but not within the last 3 — count at their total. Reports received fewer than 3 whole months before do not count as premiums.

**Q. What if none was received in that span?**
A. When none was received 3 to 11 whole months before and some were received 12 to 23 whole months before, the standard Medicare Part B premium of 202.90 a month for 12 months, for each member of the household the rate category covers, is counted instead: 2 members in a rate category that counts spouse income, 1 in a category that does not. That is 2434.80 for one member and 4869.60 for two.

**Q. And otherwise?**
A. Premiums add nothing.

| Medical expense reports received | Premiums counted |
|---|---|
| some 3 to 11 whole months before | the total of those reports |
| none 3 to 11 months before, some 12 to 23 months before | 202.90 times 12 times household members |
| neither | 0 |

*Hypothetical:* in a no-dependent category, reports of 2100.00 received 5 whole months before and 1900.00 received 15 whole months before: 2100.00 is counted. Without the 5-month report, 2434.80 is counted — and still 2434.80 if a further report was received 1 whole month before, since that report falls outside the 3-to-11-month span. With only a report 30 whole months old, nothing.
